direct_fc2.switch: DG_SM90_PREFILL_DIRECT_FC2=1 (host; with DG_SM90_PREFILL_4STAGE=1, not with the tail split) -> trailing template arguments kPrefillTailSplit=false, kPrefillDirectFC2=true
direct_fc2.design: Every 256-column FC2 block of a partial row is stored permuted: bytes 64 j + 16 c hold n8 chunks 4j..4j+3 of lane-quad position c (natural columns 32 j + 8 q + 2 c + {0,1}). Each thread writes its rows r_0 and r_1 with 8 STG.128 each straight from the accumulators. The paired combine reads the same uint4s, sums the top-k partials element by element in slot order as before and writes the y staging chunk in natural order (4 x STS.32 per uint4).
direct_fc2.exactness: bit-identical by construction (same BF16 values, same per-element FMA order, same y bytes); the selection requires bitwise equality with the control
direct_fc2.removed_work_per_fc2_tile: 64 KiB STS + 64 KiB LDS of shared-memory traffic, 8 warp syncs and the 4-step STS->LDS->STG dependency chain; straight-line span per thread 223 -> 126 instructions (STS 64 -> 0, LDS 16 -> 0, STG.128 16 = 16, F2FP 64 = 64)

gather_a.switch: DG_SM90_PREFILL_GATHER_A=1 (host; one rank, four-stage 2WG tile, not with the tail split) -> trailing kPrefillGatherA=true after kPrefillTailSplit=false and kPrefillDirectFC2
gather_a.design: The EP1 dispatch keeps the SF copy, the source metadata and the per-row arrival release but no longer pulls each 4 KiB token row through its shared-memory buffer into the L1 pool (TMA load + TMA store + two waits per row). The FC1 A loader, after acquiring a tile's arrival count, writes the tile's 128 token indices into the then unused pull buffers and per K block issues 16-byte cp.async.cg copies of the valid rows from the input token buffer: lane l copies chunk l % 8 of rows 32 (l / 8) + i, four whole 128-byte rows per instruction, at the TMA SWIZZLE_128B position (chunk ^ row % 8). Padding rows are not copied. Each lane's cp.async.mbarrier.arrive (counted form, net zero) keeps the stage's full barrier open until its copies land; the elected lane then issues the SFA TMA and the loader's single arrival with the SFA bytes. Consumers issue fence.proxy.async.shared::cta after each FC1 full-barrier wait (generic-proxy cp.async writes before async-proxy WGMMA reads). FC2 is unchanged (TMA from the FC1-output pool).
gather_a.exactness: bit-identical by construction for every valid row (same A bytes, scales, K order); padding rows hold stale bytes as before and are never stored; the selection requires bitwise equality
gather_a.removed_work: Per layer 64.5k row copies: 8 KiB of shared-memory traffic per row (3.9 MB per SM), 264 MB of HBM writes into the pool and the pool's re-read by FC1 (the 33 MB input buffer is read instead, from L2 when resident), and the A shared-memory writes of padding rows (pad128 13.4-16.0 % of FC1 A rows).

ep1_four_stage_gather.loader_pass: 57 instructions per four 16-byte copies (8 passes per K block)

gather_a.risks: The A loader now issues ~460 instructions per K block (one warp, 40 registers) instead of one TMA; input rows are re-read by up to 8 experts' tiles and may miss L2; cp.async L1 bypass traffic. Any defect shows as a bitwise mismatch (variant rejected); the barrier accounting follows the counted cp.async.mbarrier.arrive semantics, as in CUTLASS's SM90 cp.async GMMA mainloop.
